question: People chose a lung-cancer treatment, surgery or radiation, from the same figures given as survival or as deaths. What changed?
options: Fewer chose surgery hearing death rates
More chose surgery hearing death rates
answer: Fewer chose surgery hearing death rates. In a 1982 study, radiation was chosen by 18% when outcomes were framed as survival and by 44% when the same numbers were framed as deaths. Surgery's early risk sounds worse as 10% die than as 90% survive. Doctors in the study swung as much as anyone.
move: Turn every figure around and see whether your choice survives.
ask: Which decision of mine would change if I heard the same numbers the other way round?
trap: Same choices, since the figures underneath were identical.
source: McNeil et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 1982
reference: McNeil, Pauker, Sox & Tversky, On the elicitation of preferences for alternative therapies, New England Journal of Medicine 306(21), 1982
